answer: Each agent identity must post a refundable bond before it can place orders, and the bond is slashed when a dispute proves fraud. A rotating set of bonded peers checks each claim against signed receipts; a mirror copy of the receipt is kept outside the agent’s control, so deleting its history cannot erase evidence. The inlet accepts only claims linked to those receipts, while a vine of referrals grants no extra weight. A sybil attacker can still create identities, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it.
